contents.reason: This useful global trigonometric estimate is not itself a characterization of pi; the analytic product limits instead use the already published local limit sin x/x -> 1, so no result here depends on silently importing it.

contents.reason: This formulation depends on the complex exponential, which is not in either declared prerequisite closure; the page proves the requested real sine-and-cosine least-period characterization directly from its published real-analysis predecessor.

contents.reason: Polar-coordinate existence and uniqueness are coordinate-representation results rather than characterizations of pi, and their full treatment belongs with the later plane-geometry or complex-number material.

contents.name: Exercise 11.4.11(1), principal inverse tangent
contents.reason: Constructing the full inverse-tangent function and proving its range is an inverse-functions topic; only its definite-integral consequence is needed for the finite-remainder proof of the pi series.

contents.reason: The global inverse-function derivative theorem is not required here because the scaffold evaluates the relevant integral by the already published tangent substitution and quarter-turn values.
